summary: Robert S. P. Beekes worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1956–1969) under doctoral supervisor F. B. J. Kuiper (~1963–1969), and later held posts at Marnix Gymnasium and Leiden University (1973, 1979).
Robert Sewell was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1894) and was Keeper at the Tamil Nadu Archives.
Robert Seymour Conway was a linguist who studied at the City of London School (~1876–1883). He later held posts at Newnham College (~1887–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).

Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 1994, he was attested studying under doctoral supervisor Karen Christina Lang and under adviser and teacher K. L. Seshagiri Rao.

Robert Zimmermann worked in Indology, studying at St Beuno's Jesuit Spirituality Centre (~1904–1907) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1908–1913). He served as Professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930) and led the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Robert Zydenbos works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. After studying at Utrecht University (~1975–1983), he held posts at the University of Toronto, University of Munich (~2000), and Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).
Robert van Gulik specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (~1929–1934) and Utrecht University (~1934–1935) under doctoral supervisor Jan Gonda (~1930–1935).

Robin Coningham works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at King's College and the University of Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin (~1989–1994), later holding professorships at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (2005).
Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (~1975–1980) and held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University (~2002).

Robin Dunbar studied at Magdalen College School, Magdalen College (~1966–1969), and under doctoral supervisor John Hurrell Crook (~1969–1974). He later held an academic post at University College London (~1987–1994).

Roderick M. Chisholm was a philosopher who studied at Brown University (1934–1938) and Harvard University (~1938–1942). His posts included the Barnes Foundation (~1946), Brown University (~1947–1987), and the University of Graz (1974).
Roderick S. Bucknell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Queensland, attested in 1988 and as Associate Professor in 1999–2000.

Roderick Whitfield works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held positions at the British Museum (attested 1986), the University of London (attested 2010), and SOAS University of London (attested 2011, 2022).

Roger Bischoff is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers Mother Sayamagyi and U Chit Tin (attested 1995). He served as an Assistant Teacher at the International Meditation Centre (attested 1995).
Roger Brown was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at the University of Michigan (~1946–1952). He later held a post at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.

Roger Heim studied at École Centrale Paris (~1920–1923) and the Science Faculty of Paris (until 1931). He spent his career at the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle (~1929–1970), serving as its director from ~1950 to 1965.

Roger R. Jackson studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1983) under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he held posts at Fairfield University (attested 1986) and Carleton College (attested 1990–2017).

Roger T. Ames studied at UBC, CUHK, NTU, and SOAS under D. C. Lau (PhD 1975–1978). In philosophy and Sinology, he held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1978–2016) and Peking University (~2016).
Rohit Saluja is a scholar in computational fields and Indology. He has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.

Roland Barthes worked in philosophy and linguistics, studying at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1935–1941) and under Émile Benveniste (~1962–1967). He held posts at CNRS (~1952–1959), EHESS (~1962–1976), and the Collège de France (1976–1980).
